title: Paper Sorcerer
text: This is one game i picked up on a whim as i had enough in my wallet to buy it and thought "OH THIS LOOKS DIFFERENT I WILL GIVE IT A GO",and boy i am glad i did. The graphics really do,do the game justice and the way they suit the name of the game "PAPER SORCERER" is uncanny.When you are walking round the different floors of the prison you have been incarcerated in the game looks really good and flows really smoothly.It does look at times (when in fights and stationary in the sanctuary) that the art work has been drawn on paper and then transferred into the game,with the artwork reminding me of the artwork found in the old D&D books i used to read and play through with my friends when we played D&D when i was a kid.This works really well and the music in game adds to the feeling that you are actually playing a D&D board game but in actual game form,the graphics effects for spells are all ok and each one looks different. The characters you amass on your journey all look different and all have different play styles from the heavy classes which include the "MINOTAUR" who is good at heavy attacks and powerfull special attacks to the defense classes which include the "SHADOW" who has great defense magic and also spells that prevent status effects. The music in game (what is there) does a good job like i have said of putting you in that world of sword and sorcerey and never does outstay its welcome (could have done with some more sound effects in game though). The story is both entertaining and a joy to watch as it unfolds the further you progress through the tower and it is both a mysterious and wonderous journey to take as you progress from level to level.The further you get the more the enemies change and the more you have to look at your play style and change up the tactics you have been using as what worked on the floor below might not (and usually doesnt) work on the floor your on,this forces you to look at your team and make changes accordingly as you get further into the game. This brings me to the difficulty level which at first can seem quite punishing,but believe me it isnt,the more you play the game the better you get (YEAH OF COURSE DUH) and the more you learn the little intricacies the game can throw at you.Many a time i have got to the gaurdian who stops your progress to the next level just to be beaten (sometimes by my own lack of in game time to be honest) and therefore have to load up again,but then when you do you learn what he/she does and when he/she does it and what they are vulnerable to and also when they summon companions to fight you and also when they are going to use spells (some of them use certain other spells to prepare for the spell that they usually crush you with "WHY YOU PAIN IN THE A...") and with this you learn and evetually you will "CRUSH THEM AND TAKE THEIR SOULS". There are a few in game quests to do that you dont have to do to finish the game and my favorite is finding the "LOST SOULS",when you do find these you hand them in to the creepy old man who lives in the abandoned house (all by himself so run away kids if you know whats good for you) and he then opens up a level of the "REAPERS DUNGEON",these are worth doing and handing in as you get the oppertunity to explore a level of the reapers dungeon and this means you can find some really cool gear and other items that just cant be found in the main game. Will you like this game,well yes if you like a good sword and sorcery romp and have the patience to play through what can be at some times quite a tough and challenging game then by all means "STEP FORWARD ADVENTURER" if that doesnt sound like your cup of tea then look elswhere as this wont be the game for you.

title: Paper Sorcerer
text: I have played about 5 hours of the game, fought with the first three bosses. I'd most probably continue playing the game, but I just could not withstand the user interface any more. It is so bad that it's hard to describe, it has be to experienced (and I suggest you do not). It is the worst user interface I've seen in games, ever. The game itself is good enough, it has party variety, it has quite interesting enemies, and it has a few new concepts such as lowering defense during combat. I really like the fact that no matter how good your armor is, with enough effort you will cut through it eventually. Unfortunately this mechanic is not well explained and it lacks some polish and (especially) detailed explanation how it really works. But overall, the gameplay is solid. The environment is lacking, but it's still borderline good enough. What kills this game is UI. I think the developer would be in fact able to design better interfaces (just by copying what you see in ever other game you get a 100x more usable UI), but he's just not technically skilled to create it. This is his first game and he has no real programming skills. The official website even confirms it "Ultra Runaway Games was created when  one man with no industry experience or programming training decided to make a PC RPG.". And when you read his comments on forums that music volume cannot be adjusted because he doesn't know how to implement a slider, it's just... sad. Don't take me wrong, he has a courage and a passion, and if he really knew nothing about programming in the beginning, this is a very good result. But still, that doesn't make this game playable, unfortunately. The UI is simply horrible and you spend more time fighting with the UI than fighting with enemies. Even basic tasks like looking at the inventory is extremely cumbersome and slow. Battles are excruciatingly slow because of the way how you give commands. And the list goes on. There are even some bugs, but often it's just horrible UI or design decision in action. For example, you pick up a plate armor, then you look into inventory, and it's not there. WTF? You load and try it again, same result. A bug? No, a design decision to not show you any item in inventory that you cannot use at that moment. (Or at least that's what I assume it is, it is not explained anywhere). But it "appears" once you want to sell it. So much time wasted figuring this out... There are other technical issues that will slightly drive you mad, but I think most of them boil down to simply insufficient programming skills of the developer. It's unfortunate, because this is very close to the "my kind of game", but I can't recommend this at its present state. If there are some patches in the future that will completely overhaul the user interface, then sure, this can become an entertaining game. At present not worth it, though.

title: Paper Sorcerer
text: Fun little combination of a JRPG and a western dungeon-crawler RPG.  Battles are turn-based menu-style, like Final Fantasy, but the rest of the gameplay is first-person realtime exploration with plenty of looting, puzzles and dungeon crawling, like Skyrim.  The graphics and music are a charming combination of retro and modern, with a realtime 3d environment rendered in only 2 colors to give a "inside a book" feel, and some really great chiptune music.  As a plus, the story is a refreshing break from the traditional "heroes saving the world" cliche, and instead puts you in the role of an evil sorceror trying to escape his enchanted prison.  Really fun little game, definitely recommended.

title: Paper Sorcerer
text: Story of the game is pretty simple. You are an evil sorcerer that some good king sent some heroes to trap inside a prison, this groovy magic book that you (and many other evils) have been trapped inside of. You go through the levels to try and escape. You get to pick from a variety of possible team mates as you go like a Witch, Vampire, Werewolf, Minotaur, Ghost, Troll, Imp etc. You pick what you want and build a classic 4-person party. You actually get (I think) 6 slots total.  Pros: - As advertised, basically a love letter to the early wizardry games but you don't have to grind like 10 hours to get off floor 1, so, that's good. - The graphic look rules. Basically the whole world looks like black and white ink drawings, but the dungeon is a 3-D world. It's cool, if minimalist. - Honestly, the first old fashioned RPG I've actually played and been enjoying in a while - Seems to be lots of different approaches with your party. Each character offers something different. I can see playing this more than once just to test out different combinations - Has multiple difficulty levels, something a lot of RPG's don't offer - Offers a windowed mode and control remaping, both of which I roll my eyes at any PC game I encounter without them.  Cons: - This was done by (AFAIK) a one man programming team and I have hit a glitch in town twice that causes no menu options to pop up. Save often. - Speaking of saves, when you reload them all doors on a level are shut as if you just arrived. Minor annoyance. - One of the one-man-team oddities, the game has no volume controls at all. It is what it is. Some people have been (here's a shocker) very rude on the Steam forums about wanting to turn off the music. I really don't see the fuss. - The heroic knights in the opening cutscene have weird helmets that kind of make them look like Klan members.  Overall: definite thumbs up if you enjoy old school RPG's. It's not really the most complex game, but it's also not a pricey one and it will definitely kill some time. I'm definitely enjoying it. There's nothing here that will redefine a genre or do anything you haven't seen before, but it does what it does well.

title: Paper Sorcerer
text: If you're a fan of turn-based RPGs at all, you owe it to yourself to give this game a try. The most obivous difference between this game and most others is the quite unusual art style.  The team making this game is obviously on a budget, and you can see some oddball errors (like inky shadows that are actually 2d planes you can see behind if you jump into the corner) but they decided to use their limited resources to make the most visually striking game they could, regardless. The same can be said of combat, which is the real meat of the game.  The game uses pre-generated character archetypes that you add to your party in a team of your choosing.  The array of choices are unfortunately not overwhelming, and you don't get a very clear sense of who can do what until after you get them in your party, but if you save before the choice, and experiment a little, you can figure things out. Combat revolves around energy (which is used only 1-6 points at a time, and where you recover 1 per turn) and cooldowns on skills, as well as an unusual defense system.  Defense drops after physical attacks, and applies to both physical and magic attacks.  Since very high defense nullifies direct magic damage, you need to pound a target's armor down to make them vulnerable to magic.  Meanwhile, magic skills that debuff resistance to physical damage or can incapacitate a target are available, but only within the limits of energy and cooldowns.  It's a game that has unusual depth to how much you have to think to get through even regular battles. (Especially on the brutal "1980s" difficulty.) Unfortunately, the game also behaves oddly in many circumstances.  Ability cooldowns don't take as long as they say they do in the menu, and sometimes last into the next combat you engage in.  If you move the mouse while the 2d image of the town is loading, you actually make the perspective on the town move, as it's just a 2d cutout in front of the game's camera.  There's an achievement that you can't unlock because it was accidentally made inaccesible. There's also some balance issues, especially with overpowered skills like sleep, where enemies  only wake up from normal attacks, while a skeleton that's using physical skills to kill the opponent never wakes the target.  This tends to make status effect and damage-over-time characters extremely powerful, while the characters that rely upon direct magic damage are extremely weak because of the way defense works against them.

title: Particle Fleet: Emergence
text: Another excellcent game from this studio that's a little hard to classify.  It is different than the creeper world series but still feels familiar.  Instead of fighting creeper moving along the surface, you are fighting against particles that flow / shoot out of locations.  The particles travel through space based on the terrain, fields and natural forces.  There are also some other obstacles such as plasma (slows your ships), emergent (powerful somewhat random moving ship killers), mines, turrets and even enemy ships and ship like particles in latter missions. To battle this you have a small fleet and a limited land vechicle to fight this.  Each scenario defines what ships are available and each ship has a role (i.e. capturing spawn points, blocking/ramming, ranged fighting, killing ships, clearing plasma, speed, etc).  It makes for a very rewarding experience, slowly fighting back the particles and using your ships to the best of their abilities.  Very puzzle like and less RTS like.  It should also be mentioned you can build your own ships and use them in missions in sandbox mode or even make them the default ships in your own missions made with the editor. Overall I found this game easier than creeper world 3 (only creeper game I've played so far).  The story is also a bit on the short side but there are user made missions, hard missions and random missions which still gives a lot of content.  Overall, well worth your time if you are into unique strategy experiences.

title: Particle Fleet: Emergence
text: Compared to it's predacessors, Particle Fleet is a dissapointment. There is very little strategy involved, the story is forced (painfully so), and the level variety leaves a lot to be desired. Every mission its the same thing. Turtle up in the energy well, capture more energy wells, make a massive fleet, destroy particle nodes. Rinse and repeat. Creeper world, the games predeccessor, had much more variety in terms of obsatcles and weapons the player was up against, and in response the player had to adapt. In Particle fleet, there is no adapting, because you are only allowed the ships you are given, and even the particles themselves don't really seem that dangerous when your ships can take a truckload of them inside your own energy wells. You can create a custom fleet, sure, but for most, that won't make the game any harder. As for the story, I don't mind so much its shorter than it's Creeper World counterparts. I do mind that it was poorly developed with an ending so forced only a "first draft for sale on Amazon author" would be proud of it. And before fan boys begin commenting "well you only didn't like the ending because..." No. That type of ending is fine so long as it is done right. This one isn't done right. It's pointless, senseless, and it practically gives a middle finger to the player. Perhaps I wouldn't have minded so much if the gameplay was interesting, but it wasn't. TLDR: In short it's Gun platforms vs. Particle effects, and that's it. Compared to Knuckle Cracker's earlier outings, this game just feels lazy and/or a cash in on an idea they were too far along to give up on but didn't want to take all the way. Knuckle Cracker games used to be a guaranteed purchase from me. After Particle Fleet, they arn't anymore.

text: An unenthusiastic yes. I bought this game because I spent a significant amount of time with Creeper World 3 and enjoyed the gameplay and story. It took me a while before I decided to, however; the game didn't look that great. The gameplay is similar to CW3, but with obvious significant differences, and that gave me pause. Ultimately I tried it, and enjoyed the game, and then... it was done. There's very little game to this game. I blew through the 'campaign' very quickly, and the other whatever you want to call it that looks like a campaign but isn't, but while I'm still working through the hundreds of additional levels in CW3 I've completed this one in a day or two. Sure, you can design your own block-by-block ships, but the campaign does a good job of giving you the ships you need when you get them, so unless you design similar ships, good luck to you. And that's the sad thing: there's no easy way to use your own ships in a game to test them out. Randomly generate a level and it gives you a selection menu to pick from the real ships only. Launch the game, and then you can set the game mode to sandbox and pick your own ships.... but only after clearing the default loadout and manually adding your ships one by one, and don't click the wrong place or you'll be dragging ships back in order constantly afterwards. The game favors making your own ships and maps, and you -can- download maps to play made by other players, but I've had more crashes than completed games that way, and it's not like CW3 where exiting gives you an auto-save. Prepare to lose progress. Ultimately I'm disappointed. I liked going through the premade material, but that's where the game dies for me, and it's not really worth the price I paid.

title: Particle Fleet: Emergence
text: Greetings!  At its core Particle Fleet: Emergence is a simple game; sort of like playing against a virus.  You slowly capture territory and build ships while the enemy spreads out in all direction with an endless supply of particles (duh).  You will spend a good deal of time overwhelmed and barely holding on but this is part of the charm of the game. Difficult but Fair:  I almost consider this game a ‘souls-like’ game, the difficulty can be high but it is far and you will need to repeat some levels to adapt and understand the best approach.  Some tactics that work wonders on one level will be useless at another.  You have to evaluate your location, land mass, energy mines and the way your opponent is coming at you.  This ends in a satisfying victory when you do finally accomplish it and doesn’t take too long to pick up and put down. Simple and effective:  Every bit of this game is efficient and effective, no, the graphics aren’t award winning but they accomplish the game’s purpose and I’d argue that better graphics could ruin the game.  The music is amazing and although it would be nice to have a bit more I love the score that is in this game.  Mechanics are solid and so are the controls; overall just no real complaints. So, what’s bad:  I can’t really say that I have any part of this game I dislike?  Well, now that I think about it sometimes you get a point where the game is yours but it is going to take another 5-10 minutes to slowly make your way to victory.  This can be a bit boring at times but I don’t really see a way around it.  Overall, I love this game, especially for its price.  The story could be better but wasn’t really expecting anything on this front. All in all, if you like tactical games, especially those that are easy to pick up and a decent difficulty to ensure a satisfactory victory (or defeat) get this game.  It is well worth the play through and if you are like me you will find yourself picking it up from time to time.  Enjoy!

text: On the Rain-Slick Precipice of Darkness 3... what a title. In fact, the writing in this game was probably my favorite part. Constantly making clever jokes, the dialouge never got old. However, on a rainy day if you like a little dry humor this is a great way to burn time and snag a few chuckles.

title: Penny Arcade's On the Rain-Slick Precipice of Darkness 3

title: Penny Arcade's On the Rain-Slick Precipice of Darkness 3
text: Here is a game that largely matches expectations without exceeding them. If you're looking for solid, retro-RPG combat and witty writing then you'll find it here at a very reasonable price. However, the story behind all the sarcasm and jokes, while entertaining enough, lacks tension and impact. It sets up the following game for a more interesting setting and conclusion, but that's not enough to elevate game's narrative above "mostly forgettable". Precipice of Darkness 3 does a great job of bringing complexity and flexibility into its turn based combat. Each party member has one permanent base class that matches their personality. In time you'll unlock two additional class slots for each character that can be swapped at will between battles. You choose from a pool of bizarre classes that allow you to easily experiment until you find a winning combination. I really like that unused classes still gain experience and level up, just at a slightly slower pace than the in use classes. This negates the chance of any class becoming under leveled to the point of discouraging you from trying it. In battle the game uses a combat bar to queue actions that is much like the old Grandia series and, more recently, Child of Light. It is one of my favorite turn based systems that allows for characters and attacks of varying speeds as well as strategic interrupts of enemy actions. To be victorious I needed to make proper use of buffs, interrupts and adjust my strategy to account for enemy weaknesses and resistances. I played on the Veteran difficulty and found it to be on point except for in one area called The Bank of Money that had a frustrating and unusual spike in difficulty.  The city map that you use to navigate from area to area is very plain with linear paths that don't allow for any deviation or hidden surprises. The exploration areas are genre standard mazes of corridors, barriers and rooms. Their layout is pleasing, including treasure chests, non-random enemy encounters and silly descriptions when you examine some objects. Visuals are definitely not this game's strong suit. They get the job done without being outright ugly, but the best compliment I can give them is that there are some creatively comedic enemy designs. Having not played the previous two games nor read much of the Penny Arcade comics I'm coming at this game without a preexisting attachment to the characters. While I did enjoy their distinct and quirky personalities, they only grew on me a little over time. There are some decent attempts at character development, however the priority is clearly on humor over substance. As for the comedy, for me it was consistently amusing without ever being a truly laugh-out-loud level of funny. It's worth noting that I did not feel like I was missing anything from not having played parts 1 and 2.  My total playtime clocked in at 15 hours for all the content this game has to offer. It is a modestly successful entry in the relatively sparse field of games that place a heavy emphasis on comedy. I am comfortable recommending this game to any old school RPG fans out there or Penny Arcade aficionados.

title: Penny Arcade's On the Rain-Slick Precipice of Darkness 3
text: Greetings Again!  Next on the list is part three of the Rain Slick Precipice of Darkness series by Penny Arcade.    It is no secret that I am a huge fan of RPGs and especially those of the classic JRPG style and this game definitely matches the theme, but is it something I’d recommend you buy? Wall of Text:  The story resumes where it left off but with a very different feel (and a new development team from what I understand), gone are the voice over acting and everything has been brought back to a time when 16 bit was all we could do.  This includes the graphics, the audio, everything; even the menus are done in this style.  The game even has a small segment where you go 8 bit for a while.  The story does follow along the previous two but I found myself losing some of the content due to long periods of text boxes.  To be honest, I really should have just taken a bit of a break at those points. Punch-A-Thon:  Mechanically the game plays very similar to any old school RPG that you’ve seen before with a few small twists.  You don’t use mana in the same was you normally would, instead of having a mana pool that you deplete you start at zero and gain one every turn.  This moves into the second design choice, where you regain all items, health and clear all status effects at the end of the battle.  This is nice but it leads to one of the few problems I have with the game, ie battles can feel like a chore at times, leading to effectively what may feel like a never ending boss battle and have the rewards of normal encounters.  Don’t get me wrong however, if you take a 15 minute break from the game you get refreshed and are ready to jump back in. Another one bites the dust:  Complaints, well I would have liked to see random encounters (still limited by static enemy locations) but at least there is a place you can ‘grind’ a bit here and there.  Many of the classes feel less useful than the others and there seems to be a great deal of useless abilities.  Maybe that is just my play style.  The game did feel overly simplistic but so did the previous ones, this game is less of a innovation than a tribute to what came before.  Still, I regret nothing and am happy that I played to the conclusion (though I still cannot beat the Dark Clones in the secret dungeon).  I do both enjoy and am annoyed with the power escalation mechanic (enemies get stronger each turn) but it is a good way to prevent turtling, which happens to be my go to for bosses, so yeah…). If you’ve played the previous games of this series you really don’t need incentive to buy this, in fact I feel it would be silly not to, why would you leave the story unfinished?  For those of you who haven’t and am looking this as a standalone game, I’d say the game itself is worth the purchase if you can stand the fact that you are starting midway through the story, I’d really recommend buying the whole lot but to each their own, enjoy!

title: Pinball Arcade
text: There have been a ton of awesome pinball tables over the years and Pinball Arcade is one of the best programs to come along so far to deliver the experience of digital pinball with actual table designs from years gone by. Granted, if you're not into pinball, there's nothing really here for you, but without spending any money you do get full access to one table and can demo every other table without paying a dime. Very good (though not perfect) physics, table designs are nearly spot-on to the real machines, includes a mix of various tables from the most popular to the least popular, as well as from the most common to the absurdly rare, actual ROM data is being used so the tables have all of their hidden features and everything, all of which are documented in-game, extensive instructions available for every table to make learning the rulesets much easier. Default configuration and camera settings are garbage for anyone looking to REALLY play the game, so you need to reconfigure everything, the "Call Attendant" feature for dealing with issues can't handle most of the problems which crop up (which are thankfully few and far between), very expensive if you want "pro" access to all the tables (extra configuration settings and options for examining the table)... still cheaper than owning just a single REAL machine. :P

title: Pinball Arcade
text: It's not a perfect simulation of physical pinball but it's pretty solid.  The DLC (which is basically required) is NOT cheap, but pinball is a VERY expensive hobby.  Real machines run north of 10,000 USD.  So 40 USD for a table pack, even if it just contains Addams and nine tables you don't care about, isn't too bad.  If you visit the arcade or pub and spend $10 in beer, and $20 in games for a few hours, this is comparable.  Make your own value judgements here. Tables are generally on factory defaults as far as difficulty goes with respect to outlanes, rubbers, etc..  If there is an option to increase the difficulty to what you might see at a high level tournament, I've not been able to find it. The game is a good 'trainer' for learning how a given game's rules play out with respect to strategy.  For example, you can experiment here with Attack From Mars as to how multiball interacts with the Attack Wave mechanism. However, the games are still "the same" from a User Experience / general feel perspective.  Twilight Zone feels like Twilight Zone.  Rule the Universe is still incredibly hard on Attack From Mars.  Addams Family is still awesome.

title: Pink Heaven
text: This is one of the best games on Steam.  Beautiful overall game.  The music is 10/10.  The storyline is 10/10.  I got a cool umbrella in the game that let me float wherever I wanted.  I saved my blue friend, at first I was freaking out that I would never find her again.  After saving the day, I was showered with flowers.  Even the aliens that I had beef with and killed put flowers on they're space craft before flying away and we all lived happily ever after.        100/100     Highly Recommended!  Download Now!
